```{r load}
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(patchwork)
library(knitr)
library(geogrid)

analysis_lga <- read_csv(
  "clean_data/analysis_lga.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  mutate(
    region = factor(
      if_else(
        pct_pop_greater_melb > 50,
        "Greater Melbourne",
        "Regional Victoria"
      ),
      levels = c("Greater Melbourne", "Regional Victoria")
    )
  )

lga <- st_read("data/lga/LGA_POLYGON.shp", quiet = TRUE) |>
  filter(!str_detect(LGA_NAME, "UNINC")) |>
  mutate(LGA_CODE = as.numeric(LGA_CODE)) |>
  select(LGA_CODE)

map_data <- lga |> left_join(analysis_lga, by = "LGA_CODE")

outcomes <- c(
  "Inactivity" = "inactive_percent",
  "Activity" = "activity_percent",
  "Obesity" = "obesity_percent",
  "Distress" = "distress_percent",
  "Poor health" = "poor_health_percent"
)

access <- c(
  "Park distance" = "med_dist_park_m",
  "Natural-area distance" = "med_dist_nature_m",
  "Facility distance" = "med_dist_facility_m",
  "Indoor-facility distance" = "med_dist_indoor_m",
  "Indoor-facility share" = "pct_indoor_facilities",
  "Sport types" = "sport_type_count"
)

region_cols <- c(
  "Greater Melbourne" = "#2C7FB8",
  "Regional Victoria" = "#F28E2B"
)
```

```{r paried map}
paired_map <- function(data, fill_var, widths = c(1, 1.4)) {
  var_name <- rlang::as_name(rlang::ensym(fill_var))

  legend_name <- names(c(outcomes, access))[
    match(var_name, c(outcomes, access))
  ]

  is_outcome <- var_name %in% outcomes
  is_distance <- grepl("distance", legend_name, ignore.case = TRUE)

  metro_bbox <- st_bbox(filter(data, region == "Greater Melbourne"))

  base <- ggplot(data) +
    geom_sf(
      aes(fill = {{ fill_var }}),
      colour = "white",
      linewidth = 0.1
    ) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(
      option = if (is_outcome) "magma" else "viridis",
      direction = if (is_outcome) -1 else 1,
      trans = if (is_distance) "log10" else "identity"
    ) +
    labs(
      fill = if (is_outcome) {
        "%"
      } else if (is_distance) {
        "Metres"
      } else {
        legend_name
      }
    ) +
    theme_void()

  p_vic <- base +
    labs(title = "Victoria")

  p_mel <- base +
    coord_sf(
      xlim = metro_bbox[c("xmin", "xmax")],
      ylim = metro_bbox[c("ymin", "ymax")],
      expand = FALSE
    ) +
    labs(title = "Greater Melbourne")

  (p_vic | p_mel) +
    patchwork::plot_layout(
      widths = widths,
      guides = "collect"
    ) +
    patchwork::plot_annotation(
      title = legend_name
    ) &
    theme(legend.position = "right")
}
```

```{r hexagon map}
map_projected <- map_data |> st_transform(7899)

hex_grid <- calculate_grid(
  shape = map_projected,
  grid_type = "hexagonal",
  seed = 1
)

hex_data <- assign_polygons(map_projected, hex_grid)

reverse_vars <- c("activity_percent", "pct_indoor_facilities", "sport_type_count")

dist_vars   <- access[grepl("distance", names(access), ignore.case = TRUE)]
dist_limits <- range(unlist(sf::st_drop_geometry(hex_data)[dist_vars]), na.rm = TRUE)
dist_breaks <- c(200, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000, 20000)
dist_labels <- c("200 m", "500 m", "1 km", "2 km", "5 km", "20 km")

hex_map <- function(data, fill_var, limits = NULL) {
  var_name   <- rlang::as_name(rlang::ensym(fill_var))
  variables  <- c(outcomes, access)
  title_text <- names(variables)[match(var_name, variables)]

  is_outcome  <- var_name %in% outcomes
  is_distance <- var_name %in% dist_vars

  dir <- if (var_name %in% reverse_vars) 1 else -1

  fill_scale <- if (is_distance) {
    scale_fill_viridis_c(
      option = "viridis", direction = -1,
      transform = "log10",
      limits = dist_limits, breaks = dist_breaks, labels = dist_labels,
      name = "Median distance"
    )
  } else {
    scale_fill_viridis_c(
      option    = if (is_outcome) "magma" else "viridis",
      direction = dir,
      limits    = limits,
      oob       = scales::squish,
      name      = if (grepl("percent|pct", var_name)) "%" else "Count"
    )
  }

  ggplot(data) +
    geom_sf(aes(fill = {{ fill_var }}), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
    fill_scale +
    coord_sf(datum = NA) +
    labs(title = title_text) +
    theme_void() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
      legend.position = "right"
    )
}
```

# Exploratory Data Analysis

This exploratory analysis examines variation in recreational accessibility and health outcomes across Victoria's 79 local government areas. We first describe the distributions and spatial patterns of the outcome and accessibility measures, then assess their unadjusted associations. We also explore how socioeconomic advantage and population density relate to these measures, as well as correlations among predictors. Finally, we compare patterns between Greater Melbourne and Regional Victoria to explore potential regional differences.

All six accessibility indicators and five health outcomes are included in the descriptive and correlation analyses. For readability, the main text displays selected maps and scatterplots where the visual patterns are most informative.

## Variation in Health Outcomes Across Victorian LGAs

```{r}
#| label: fig-health-distributions
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of five age standardised health outcome estimates across 79 Victorian LGAs. Each point represents one LGA."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.5
analysis_lga |>
  select(all_of(unname(outcomes))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "outcome", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(
    outcome = factor(
      names(outcomes)[match(outcome, outcomes)],
      levels = rev(names(outcomes))
    )
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(value, outcome)) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.7) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0, height = 0.14, alpha = 0.45, size = 1.5) +
  labs(
    x = "Estimated percentage of adults",
    y = NULL,
    title = "Distribution of Health Outcomes"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10)
```

@fig-health-distributions shows the distributions of five age-standardised health outcomes across Victoria's 79 LGAs. Obesity shows a relatively wide spread, with estimates ranging from approximately 10% to 35%, while insufficient physical activity ranges from around 4% to 26%. The percentage of adults achieving at least 150 minutes of moderate to vigorous physical activity (MVPA) per week is more concentrated, with the middle 50% of LGAs ranging from approximately 32% to 37%. However, a few LGAs have substantially higher estimates, reaching around 51%. Psychological distress and fair or poor self-rated health show narrower distributions than obesity.

```{r}
#| label: fig-inactivity-hex
#| fig-cap: "Hexagon tile map showing the spatial distribution of insufficient physical activity across Victorian LGAs. Each hexagon represents one LGA with equal visual area."
hex_map(hex_data, inactive_percent)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-obesity-hex
#| fig-cap: "Hexagon tile map showing the spatial distribution of obesity across Victorian LGAs. Each hexagon represents one LGA with equal visual area."
hex_map(hex_data, obesity_percent)
```

@fig-inactivity-hex and @fig-obesity-hex show spatial variation in insufficient activity and obesity across Victorian LGAs, with each hexagon representing one LGA. Physical inactivity shows a concentration of LGAs with moderate estimates, alongside several with noticeably lower values. Obesity shows a wider range of estimates, with clearer differences between some LGAs. These two outcomes were selected to illustrate variation in both physical activity behaviour and health status.


## Variation in Recreational Accessibility Across Victorian LGAs

```{r}
#| label: fig-access-distributions
#| fig-cap: "Distributions of six recreational accessibility indicators across Victorian LGAs on their original scales."
analysis_lga |>
  select(all_of(unname(access))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "indicator") |>
  mutate(
    indicator = names(access)[match(indicator, access)],
    indicator = factor(indicator, levels = c(
      "Park distance",
      "Natural-area distance",
      "Facility distance",
      "Indoor-facility distance",
      "Indoor-facility share",
      "Sport types"
    ))
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(value)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 16, fill = "grey45", colour = "white") +
  facet_wrap(~indicator, scales = "free", ncol = 2) +
  labs(x = "Value", y = "Number of LGAs") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10)
```

@fig-access-distributions shows the distributions of all six recreational accessibility indicators across the 79 LGAs. The four distance indicators are right-skewed, with most LGAs having relatively short distances and a few showing much longer distances. Park distance has the lowest median (271 m), while indoor-facility distance has the highest (1,605 m), suggesting that parks are generally more accessible than indoor recreational facilities. The large differences between the median and maximum distances in some indicators also suggest considerable variation across LGAs.

Indoor-facility share and sport-type count capture different aspects of recreational provision. The median indoor-facility share is 16%, indicating that indoor facilities make up a relatively small proportion of recreational facilities in a typical LGA, while the median of 27 sport types suggests a range of sporting opportunities. Detailed descriptive statistics for all six accessibility indicators are provided in Appendix Table A.2.

```{r}
#| label: fig-access-hex
#| fig-cap: "Hexagon tile maps of median distances to parks, natural areas, recreational facilities and indoor recreational facilities across Victorian LGAs. All four maps use a common colour scale, and each hexagon represents one LGA with equal visual area."
(hex_map(hex_data, med_dist_park_m) + hex_map(hex_data, med_dist_nature_m)) /
  (hex_map(hex_data, med_dist_facility_m) +
    hex_map(hex_data, med_dist_indoor_m)) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect")
```

@fig-access-hex compares the spatial patterns of four recreational distance indicators across Victorian LGAs using a common colour scale. Park distances are relatively short across most LGAs, with one particularly high value in West Wimmera, where the median distance reaches approximately 19.5 km. In contrast, longer natural-area distances appear in several LGAs spread across different parts of the hex map, showing a different pattern from park distance.

Distances to recreational facilities are also relatively short for most LGAs, while indoor facilities show much longer distances in several areas. This suggests that relatively close access to recreational facilities does not necessarily mean similarly close access to indoor facilities.

### A2.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-access-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Summary statistics for six recreational accessibility indicators across 79 Victorian LGAs."
#| include: false
analysis_lga |>
  select(all_of(unname(access))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "indicator") |>
  group_by(indicator) |>
  summarise(Median = median(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            Q1 = quantile(value, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
            Q3 = quantile(value, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
            Min = min(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            Max = max(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(indicator = names(access)[match(indicator, access)]) |>
  arrange(match(indicator, names(access))) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 0, col.names = c("Indicator", "Median", "Q1", "Q3", "Min", "Max"))
```
